data.title: U.S. Stocks Moving Sharply Lower As Anthropic Plunges
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Stocks have moved sharply lower over the course of the trading session on Friday, extending the sell-off seen in the previous session. The tech-heavy Nasdaq has shown a particularly steep decline, plunging to its lowest levels in seven months.

Currently, the Nasdaq is just off its lows of the session, down 701.48 points or 2.9 percent at 23,177.72. The S&P 500 is also down 117.04 points or 1.6 percent at 7,058.79, while the narrower Dow is posting a more modest loss, down 73.24 points or 0.2 percent at 49,023.82.

The sell-off on Wall Street comes amid continued weakness among technology stocks, as reflected by the steep drop by the Nasdaq.

A steep drop by shares of Anthropic (ANT) is weigh on the tech sector following its record-breaking initial public offering on Thursday.

Shares of Anthropic are plunging by more than 10 percent after the Claude developer spiked by 17.1 percent on Thursday but ended the day well off its highs of the session.

'The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com.

She added, 'The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run.'

Concerns about the outlook for interest rates may also be contributing to the selling pressure, with at least a quarter point rate hike seen as a near-certainty at the Federal Reserve's monetary policy next month.

Following hawkish comments from several Fed officials, traders have grown increasingly worried the central bank will continue to raise rates in the coming months in order to combat stubborn inflation.

Sector News

Semiconductor stocks are turning in some of the market's worst performances on the day, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeting by 7.9 percent.

Computer hardware and networking stocks are also seeing substantial weakness, dragging the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index and the NYSE Arca Networking Index down by 6.9 percent and 6.3 percent, respectively.

Outside of the tech sector, gold stocks are extending the recent sell-off amid an extended nosedive by the price of the precious metal. Reflecting the weakness in the sector, the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index has plunged by 3.1 percent.

Brokerage, oil service and airline stocks are also seeing considerable weakness, while housing and telecom stocks are bucking the downtrend.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved sharply lower during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index dove by 5.1 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index tumbled by 1.2 percent.

The major European markets have also shown significant moves to the downside. While the German DAX Index is down by 2.3 percent, the French CAC 40 Index is down by 1.6 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index is down by 0.8 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have moved substantially higher amid the extended sell-off on Wall Street. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, is down by 10.2 basis points at 4.950 percent.

data.title: Citi Undercounted $35 Billion in Assets at U.K. Subsidiary — WSJ
data.description:
By Joe Wallace and Gina Heeb

Citigroup underestimated the size of a U.K. subsidiary by $35 billion after mistakes in how it dealt with trades, said people familiar with the matter.

After spotting the problem, the U.S. bank injected extra capital into the subsidiary over the summer, a spokeswoman said in a statement.

The record-keeping blunder is a setback for Chief Executive Jane Fraser's attempt to draw a line under Citi's history of unforced errors. In her almost six years in charge, Fraser has tried to upgrade and streamline Citi's hodgepodge of internal controls and data systems, which landed the bank in the penalty box with regulators.

Citi said it "identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary" this summer. The bank said that even before it responded, the unit's capital never fell below minimum levels required by regulators.

The bank didn't specify how the models misfired. But the mistake related to its calculation of "risk-weighted assets," a banking regulatory measure used to calculate how much capital lenders need to hold aside as a buffer against losses. The riskier the loan or security, the more capital they have to keep.

Reuters earlier reported about Citigroup's shortfall.

The Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency fined Citi $400 million and ordered the bank to fix its risk-management systems in 2020.

That spurred a turnaround program. This May, Fraser told investors that the bank had completed about 90% of the work and that the remainder focused on data governance for regulatory reporting.

"We have better risk-management practices and processes that allow us to assess exposures in real time," she said. "Our monitoring, reporting and stress testing are faster, more dynamic."

But Citi has yet to achieve its goal of persuading the Fed and OCC to remove orders they enforced six years ago, which limit its ability to do deals.

Regulators have spent well over a decade trying to make sure the internal models some big banks use to calculate risk-weighted assets give a fair reflection of their balance sheets. Banks typically strive to hold less capital, because that frees resources to make more loans.

Big international banks such as Citi face capital requirements all over the world as well as in their home market. Investors also follow risk-weighted assets closely when measuring how profitable banks are.

Citi's controls issues are the legacy of a splurge of deals the bank did in the decades before the financial crisis, when the lender wanted to become a financial supermarket. Those acquisitions included purchases in Europe. Citi remains a major player in investment banking and trading in the U.K. and on the Continent.

The bank's broker dealer in London, Citigroup Global Markets Ltd., trades stocks, bonds, commodities and derivatives. It is one of Citi's four main booking hubs globally and recorded $555 billion in total assets at the end of 2025.

The subsidiary's annual report for last year says managers maintain "disciplined oversight of earnings, capital, liquidity and risk-weighted asset efficiency." King Charles awarded Fraser, who was born in Scotland, a damehood for services to the financial sector earlier this year.

The Bank of England, which regulates the broker-dealer subsidiary, declined to comment.

Previous missteps in the U.S. include Citigroup's accidental $900 million payment to creditors of cosmetics company Revlon in 2020.

Citi's problems have landed it in hot water with European regulators as well as their American counterparts. In 2022, a London trader entered a "fat-fingered trade," as it is known in the industry — a sale for $444 billion in stocks instead of $58 million. European markets briefly crashed. U.K. watchdogs fined Citi and faulted the bank for allowing the trader to override a pop-up alert manually.

Write to Joe Wallace at joe.wallace@wsj.com and Gina Heeb at gina.heeb@wsj.com

data.title: US Justice Department drops appeal in Alaska Senate suit
data.description:
By Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff

The US Justice Department dropped its appeal on Thursday in its attempt to block certification of this month's Alaska Senate election after Democratic challenger Mary Peltola secured more than 50% of the vote.

The race was called on Tuesday, two weeks after the election, with the count showing Peltola leading by four percentage points.

  • The Justice Department had sought to preemptively delay certification of the vote in a lawsuit filed before the midterms, so it could probe whether a candidate with a similar name to Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan had led to voter confusion

  • A federal judge had said the government had no such authority

  • In Thursday's filing, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward asked the appeals court to dismiss the case, as the government "reluctantly" acknowledged that there was no viable path to investigate the vote with the ballots already counted and no longer identifiable

  • He also asked the appeals court to vacate the lower court's ruling

  • The closely watched Senate race became the subject of controversy after The New York Times reported days before the vote that Peltola's campaign recruited a retired school teacher named Dan J. Sullivan

  • The government has also launched a criminal probe into whether that recruitment effort was an illegal attempt to confuse voters

  • Peltola has said she had no part in or knowledge of the reported effort

data.title: VistaPrint Partners with Acclaimed Restaurateurs Sohla and Ham El-Waylly for Opening of Brooklyn’s Triangle Bar
data.description:
VistaPrint, the print and design partner to millions of small businesses, today announced a partnership with award-winning chefs and culinary personalities, Sohla and Ham El-Waylly, to support the opening of their newest Brooklyn venture, Triangle Bar. Additional Triangle Bar partners include Anoop Pillarisetti and Michael Tuiach.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120304334/en/

VistaPrint Partners with Acclaimed Restaurateurs Sohla and Ham El-Waylly for Opening of Brooklyn’s Triangle Bar

Located at the base of Fort Greene’s iconic triangular Fowler Square and opening in winter 2026–27, Triangle Bar is reimagining the classic neighborhood bar as a welcoming, all-occasion gathering place. The husband-and-wife duo invite guests to settle in over a pint, enjoy a comforting dinner, or linger over drinks with friends. The bar sits alongside the group’s Brooklyn restaurant, Strange Delight, a critically acclaimed, New Orleans-inspired seafood restaurant and cocktail bar in Fort Greene.

Sohla and Ham partnered with VistaPrint early in the planning process to create a consistent look and feel across every customer-facing touchpoint, including custom-printed sandwich deli paper, signature coasters, menus, takeout packaging and branded signage, t-shirts and hats.

"So much hard work goes into building a small business. Using custom print products is essential when you're trying to build an identity people remember, and we wanted every detail at Triangle Bar to feel intentional,” said Sohla and Ham El-Waylly. “When we opened Strange Delight, coordinating orders across multiple vendors while maintaining quality was exhausting. Having VistaPrint as our one-stop shop for all things branding completely streamlined the process. We're so excited to share Triangle Bar with the Fort Greene community.”

The partnership reflects VistaPrint’s ongoing commitment to championing food and beverage entrepreneurs by providing cohesive, high-quality marketing that turn brands into community destinations from opening day and beyond.

“Sohla and Ham are two of the culinary world’s most trusted voices, embodying the creativity and resilience required to build something completely their own,” said Heather Deschenes, Vice President, North America Marketing at VistaPrint. “Food and beverage branding and marketing live in tangible details that guests interact with every day. By serving as an end-to-end partner for Triangle Bar, VistaPrint makes it easy for entrepreneurs to bring their vision to life.”

For more information about the partnership and to explore the products used for the opening of Triangle Bar, click here.

About VistaPrint

VistaPrint is the print and design partner to millions of small businesses and households around the world. We help small business owners bring their ideas to life through custom print products, easy-to-use digital tools and expert design support. VistaPrint is a Cimpress company ().

data.title: Hilbert Group agrees to principles for extension of convertible notes with Helena and has been informed of a debt purchase by principal shareholder Russell Thompson
data.description:
Hilbert Group AB (publ) (“Hilbert” or the “Company”) has reached a high-level agreement with Helena Global Investment Opportunities 1 Ltd. (“Helena”) to extend the term of the convertible notes held by Helena. The extension, including the corresponding extension of the conversion rights, is subject to a final agreement being reached and the approval by an extraordinary general meeting of the Company.

Russell Thompson, Group CIO and principal shareholder, has also informed the company that he is buying USD 750,000 of the convertible notes from Helena.

The agreement covers convertible notes with a current aggregate outstanding principal amount of approximately SEK 48.9 million, excluding interest. Subject to shareholder approval, the maturity date of the notes with a nominal value of approximately SEK 21.3 million currently falling due on 10 May 2027 will be extended to 10 May 2028, and and the maturity date of the notes with a nominal value of approximately SEK 27.6 million currently falling due on 26 August 2027 will be extended to 26 August 2028.

The extension defers the Company’s repayment obligations on the affected notes, strengthening the Company’s financial flexibility as it executes its business plan. Extending the notes’ maturities means this path is not interrupted by the repayment obligations related to the notes falling due in the interim.

As part of the agreement with Helena, Hilbert will issue 6,250,000 warrants to Helena as collateral, which may only be exercised upon an event of default under the financing arrangement, with any value realised credited against the outstanding debt. This replaces the collateral that was previously agreed to be held in cash/crypto as part of the original agreement.

Barnali Biswal, Group CEO of Hilbert, comments: “This extension gives us time to execute our plan without repayment pressure which is also something shareholders have been concerned about. We appreciate Helena’s continued support. Russell’s decision to take on part of the notes personally is what made the agreement possible.”

Participation from person discharging managerial responsibilities (PDMR)

A condition for Helena agreeing to the extension was a reduction in its debt exposure to Hilbert. The Company has been informed that its principal shareholder, Russell Thompson, has acquired debt owed by Hilbert to Helena with an aggregate nominal principal amount of USD 750,000.

The acquisition is a transaction between Russell Thompson and Helena and it is paid for by Russell Thompson personally. Consequently, it does not change the Company’s total debt or bring in new funds. The Board sees Russell Thompson’s willingness to take on this exposure, on top of his existing shareholding, as a sign of his confidence in the Company’s plan.

Russell Thomson, Group CIO of Hilbert, comments: “I am buying these notes because I believe in what we are building at Hilbert. My interests are already tied to the Company through my shareholding. This adds to that exposure, and I am comfortable doing that.”

The extension will take effect only following approval by the extraordinary general meeting. Further details of the proposed extension will be set out in the notice convening the meeting, which is expected to be published within the next few weeks.

data.title: TPG-backed Newquest sells Rs 115-crore Shadowfax stake; Gallantt Ispat promoter offloads 0.66%
data.description:
Newquest Asia Fund, owned by global private equity firm TPG, sold nearly Rs 115 crore worth of shares in Shadowfax Technologies, the Bengaluru-headquartered third-party logistics company, through open-market transactions on November 20.

The stock appeared to react to the transaction, declining 2.02 percent to Rs 307.25 after touching a record high of Rs 315.25 during the trading session.

Newquest Asia Fund IV (Singapore) offloaded 37.28 lakh equity shares in Shadowfax, representing 0.63 percent of the company's paid-up equity, for Rs 114.83 crore. The shares were sold at an average price of Rs 308 apiece.

This was the fund's second stake sale in Shadowfax during the current quarter. Earlier, on October 6, it sold 40 lakh shares, representing a 0.68 percent stake, for Rs 114.8 crore.

Following the latest transaction, Newquest Asia Fund's shareholding in the logistics company declined to around 6.04 percent from 7.35 percent at the end of September 2026.

Gallantt Ispat promoter offloads 0.66% stake

Meanwhile, Dinesh R Agarwal, promoter of Gallantt Ispat, sold another 16.1 lakh equity shares in the iron and steel producer, equivalent to 0.66 percent of its total paid-up equity, for Rs 84.36 crore. The shares were sold at an average price of Rs 523.93 apiece.

On the other side of the transaction, Shree Surabhi Flour Mills acquired 5.5 lakh shares for Rs 28.76 crore at Rs 523 apiece, while Suryalaxmi Infracon purchased 10.6 lakh shares for Rs 55.6 crore at Rs 524.41 apiece.

With Friday's transaction, Dinesh Agarwal has sold a total of 1.36 crore equity shares, representing a 5.64 percent stake, during the current quarter. This is against the 5.81 percent stake held by him, as per the latest shareholding pattern.

Meanwhile, Suryalaxmi Infracon has acquired 1.06 crore shares, representing 4.4 percent of Gallantt Ispat's paid-up equity, during the current quarter.

Gallantt Ispat shares ended at Rs 538.10 on the National Stock Exchange, down 0.16 percent.

data.title: Flesh-eating screwworm cases surge in US, keeping ranchers on alert
data.description:
Key points:
  • USDA confirmed 149 screwworm cases in domestic animals since June
  • Warm, wet weather encouraged pest to spread this autumn
  • Screwworms likely to survive winter in parts of southwestern US
  • USDA restarted imports of Mexican cattle in August

By Tom Polansek and Heather Schlitz

US infestations of New World screwworm, a parasitic fly that eats warm-blooded animals alive and threatens the cattle herd, have surged in unusually wet and warm weather in the Southwest, the US Department of Agriculture and state veterinarians said.

Screwworms infested 64 cattle, dogs, horses and other domesticated animals this month, up from 34 in October and three in September, according to USDA data.

The agency has reported 149 total cases in domesticated animals since June, along with two in wild elk. Of those, 73 cases were active as of Thursday, up from two at the end of September.

Ranchers fear cases will continue to climb because there is a shortage of sterile flies that are bred to combat screwworm flies.

"The swarm has not reached Texas yet," said Susan Storey, a South Texas rancher.

USDA is racing to expand sterile fly production capacity, with the Army Corps of Engineers overseeing construction of a fly plant in South Texas due to open next year. USDA Under Secretary Dudley Hoskins told Reuters that a project to test genetically modified sterile flies that could potentially aid its response was progressing.

The agency first detected screwworm in a calf in Texas in June after the parasite marched north through Mexico, and later confirmed more cases in Texas and New Mexico. Following a lull, screwworms last month spread to Arizona, which now has nine active cases across four counties.

Screwworms encroached on Arizona from the south and east, said Dr. Ryan Wolker, state veterinarian. "The major contributing factor is the natural progression of the pest and the limited supply of sterile male screwworm flies," he said.

GENETICALLY ENGINEERED STERILE FLIES

USDA is releasing all available sterile flies in the southwestern US and around Mexico's northern border to contain infestations, while screwworms are still multiplying farther south. Sterile males mate with wild females, whose eggs then fail to hatch.

"There was a good bit of Mexico where we didn't have a good barrier of sterile flies to stop that natural progression," said Dr. Samantha Holeck, New Mexico's state veterinarian. "Now it's right there at the border — both sides of the border."

Researchers in Panama have made progress testing sterile flies genetically engineered to produce only males, which could give USDA an edge in the battle against screwworms, Hoskins said. The flies, known as NovoFly, could double the production of sterile flies by eliminating females, which are not useful in eradication efforts, he said.

"To date, all the signs and signals indicate progress and a strong competitiveness of the NovoFly in the wild," Hoskins said. "The tests so far have demonstrated everything we were hoping they would."

USDA intends to produce NovoFly at the facility scheduled to open in Texas in April, if testing continues to go well, Hoskins said. He added that it will take time to ramp up production.

The agency restarted cattle imports from Mexico at ports of entry in Arizona and New Mexico in August, after blocking them last year in an attempt to keep screwworms out. The halt helped push US beef prices to record highs for consumers.

The imports did not cause cases to spike because Mexican cattle are inspected multiple times for screwworm before entering the US, according to Hoskins, Wolker and Holeck.

Instead, rain linked to El Niño created favorable conditions for screwworms to spread, experts said, with Hurricanes Rachel and Polo bringing increased late-season moisture to Arizona and Mexico.

"As this spreads, it just exacerbates the need for more sterile flies," said David Anderson, agricultural economist at Texas A&M University.

This winter, temperatures will likely not drop low enough to kill screwworms in parts of Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, veterinarians said. That means ranchers, hunters and pet owners must watch closely for more cases.

"We're all nervous," said John Sewell, owner of a 40-square-mile deer-hunting ranch in South Texas. "You can only hope the USDA plan is working."

data.title: Nestle Eyes Autonomous Factory Lines and Looks to Google, Microsoft as Partners — Update
data.description:
By Aimee Look

ORBE, Switzerland--Swiss food giant Nestle is targeting autonomous factory lines in the future, as the maker of KitKat chocolates and Nescafe coffee teams up with big tech companies to deploy artificial intelligence.

The endgame? Getting factory lines to run themselves, Nestle's technology chief, Stefan Palzer, said in an interview.

"You need the big guys, who have the best capabilities, who have the best hardware and software solutions," he said, after Nestle opened a tech facility in Orbe, Switzerland, on Friday.

Nestle has signed partnership agreements with Microsoft and Boston Dynamics to develop AI and engineering solutions at its new Deep Tech facility. It is also in the final rounds of discussions with Google for a partnership, and leveraging some of Apple's spatial computing technology too, he added.

The company's eventual aim with these tech deals is to drive business growth, Palzer said.

With sensors and AI, Nestle's lines can fully understand and adapt to variable inputs and produce consistent output. Using the partnerships to develop an agentic AI workflow in the future would also be necessary to have automated lines, Palzer said, referring to the technology that can make decisions without much human supervision.

"At a certain point in time--we're not there yet--you can put agentic AI on top of it, and then it's orchestrating the entire flow," he said. "The fully autonomous line is one of the future. We will still need our experts, because we need expert judgment in most cases."

There will always be humans making decisions, Nestle's chief executive officer, Philipp Navratil, said.

To implement automated manufacturing workflows, Nestle needs to consider them category by category, Palzer said. His team is currently looking at unit operations to make them autonomous.

"We now do unit by unit, and we're focusing here on our top ten [manufacturing] processes," Palzer said. "We're not far away."

Developing factory lines for the food industry is different, for example, from other sorts of manufacturing like the car industry--where inputs are more uniform--said Judith Arfsten, who is head of Nestle's Deep Tech Center. For example, a hotter-than-usual summer can lead to completely different natural raw materials in a given time. Tech will work to enable the use of AI, smart sensors and robotics to improve operational efficiency.

Using AI is part of Nestle's broader strategy of identifying new ways to better understand changing consumer habits. Unpredictability around customer behavior is heightened due to weight-loss drugs and pressure on household budgets, and many companies in the sector are looking to AI for guidance.

A key question is how Nestle and other food companies can use innovation to actually drive sales, particularly for GLP-1 consumers, Vontobel analyst Jean-Philippe Bertschy said. "Technology can help with reformulation and product development, but execution will matter more than the tools," he said.

Partners including Microsoft and Boston Dynamics, which confirmed their cooperation, will help provide hardware and AI capabilities to improve both factory processes and consumer-facing products like coffee machines. The company also aims to advance its digital and hardware processes, and agreed with IBM in 2025 to use AI for packaging innovation.

The center in Orbe is also going to complement Nestle's work at its Shenzhen hub, where it seeks to identify Chinese tech it can use in products around the world.

Write to Aimee Look at aimee.look@wsj.com
